# fastf 3.17.0: what a project is, when it was last alive, and what happened lately

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed. A project nobody describes writes the same bytes it always did.

## The description

Every project can now carry **one line saying what it is** — for whom, what
for, where it stands — and every list shows it.

- `fastf desc ID0047 "Music video for Lullaby, Indie, due in May"` sets it,
  `fastf desc ID0047` prints it, `--clear` removes it.
- `fastf new --description="…"` writes it at creation, and so does `fastf
  register --description="…"` for one folder. In the app, the wizard asks it
  as its last question, after the template's own; the register form asks it
  for one folder and not for a whole base.
- In the pane it is the row under the name: Enter or F2 opens the line in
  place, emptied and Enter removes it. It wraps like a note; nothing is cut.
- `fastf recent --plain` and `fastf search --plain` print it on a row of its
  own under the project, `fastf show` under the name, and the JSON carries it
  as `description`. Free-text search matches it, and `description=*fiverr*`
  addresses it by name.

It is one line and at most 200 characters, and a refusal names the rule, on
the command line and in the pane alike. It lives in the frontmatter as
`description:` and rides in the base's index like the tags, so a list never
opens a file for it; `show`, `desc` and the pane read the file, and a line
typed into the file by hand shows in the list once the project is opened or
the base reindexed.

A template that declares a variable called `description` keeps
`--description` for that variable, as it has always been, and says so: a
script written before this release goes on working.

## Touched

Beside `created`, every project now says **when it was last written**:
`touched`, the newer of its `PROJECT_INFO.md` and its folder. It is in the
plain list, in `fastf show`, in the pane's facts and in the JSON, as the same
fixed-width stamp as `created`, so the two compare as text. It is never
stored: every write fastf makes moves it, and so does a file dropped into or
taken out of the folder's top level; an edit deeper in the folder does not,
which is why a note is still how work is said to have happened. `fastf show
--json` also carries `last_note`, the newest dated note.

## The journal

`fastf journal` is **every project's notes as one timeline**, newest first:
the day and time, the project's id, the note. `--since` is about the note's
own date, so a new note on an old project is in this month's journal;
`--template`, `--tag` and `--base` choose the projects; `--grep` keeps the
notes whose text contains a word, which is how a note written to be found
later — `lesson: ask for the stems first` — is found; `-n` sets how many, and
`--json` prints them for a script.

`docs/projects.md` now has a section on a project as memory: the three kinds
of note that outlive a project and where each is promoted to, and the two
edits that close a project.
